subject: ISV runtime compatibility pact - GuideSys SDK & tracing alignment
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ana Ruiz <ana@guidesys.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: ISV runtime compatibility pact - GuideSys SDK & tracing alignment

Hi Ana —

Following up on last week's intro: GuideSys mentioned an evaluation of multiple integrations across SDKs and tracing hooks. We support ingesting telemetry from several adapter patterns, but before we draft the formal SOW we want to map out a minimal compatibility pact that covers: SDK wiring (Lang-like adapters), trace propagation (span/key conventions), and prompt-level fidelity requirements for reproducing customer results.

Can you share a quick compatibility matrix of the GuideSys SDK variants (node/py/go) and which tracing primitives you currently emit? I attached a simple template that we can fill together. If it helps, I can propose the smallest set of guarantees we'd expect from an ISV to be Redwood-compatible for our curated catalog.

High level asks:
- Which SDKs you plan to support for GA and for early beta?
- Do your SDKs expose a pluggable tracer or do you emit OpenTelemetry spans?
- Any prompt templating layers that alter input tokenization (we've seen this cause eval drift)

If you prefer a short call, I can set up a 30-min alignment with Vanessa (partner ops) and Marissa (SDK onboarding).

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Integrations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: guideys-compat-matrix.xlsx (Excel, 28KB)]

From: Ana Ruiz <ana@guidesys.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Partner Success <partners@guidesys.ai>
Date: 2026-04-22T10:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ISV runtime compatibility pact - GuideSys SDK & tracing alignment

Hi Karthik —

Thanks for the clear note and the template — that helps. Quick answers inline:

- SDKs: Node and Python are GA; Go is experimental (internal alpha).
- Tracing: We emit OpenTelemetry spans from the runtime by default and have a pluggable exporter. We also attach a request_id and conversation_id at the top level.
- Prompt templating: We ship a templating layer that can modify whitespace and do macro expansion. We track the raw prompt and the rendered prompt but we know that change can affect tokenization.

I'm attaching our initial pass at the matrix. We'd like to aim for the "compat-lite" profile you mentioned so partners can certify quickly. Would Tuesday 4/28 at 09:30 PT work for a sync? Vanessa and Marissa joining sounds great.

Best,
Ana Ruiz
Head of Integrations
GuideSys
[Attachment: guideys-compat-matrix-filled.xlsx (Excel, 45KB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ana Ruiz <ana@guidesys.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-22T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ISV runtime compatibility pact - GuideSys SDK & tracing alignment

Ana —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the filled matrix. I reviewed the Go flag and the OpenTelemetry exporter — that aligns well with our expectations. Two follow-ups before the call:

1) Can you add an explicit row indicating whether the SDK preserves token boundaries when using templating (raw vs rendered token output)? That's the single biggest source of eval drift we've seen.
2) For traceability: we recommend an explicit span attribute "redwood.request_token_count" and a stable trace_id mapping so our cost attribution can match across systems. It's not a blocker but it makes telemetry reconciliation much faster.

I've attached a draft "compat-lite" checklist (proposed minimal guarantees) and a stub SOW for an integration pilot (Redwood proposes a lightweight QA + acceptance test suite run by both teams). Can Vanessa take the lead on SOW ops and timelines? Marissa, Mateo — can you bring a short onboarding checklist for the call (30-min) so we leave with clear next steps?

Proposed call: Tue 2026-04-28 09:30 PT (30 min). I'll send an invite.

Thanks,
Karthik
[Attachment: redwood-compat-lite-checklist.xlsx, redwood-proposed-sow-v1.pdf]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ana Ruiz <ana@guidesys.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-22T14:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ISV runtime compatibility pact - GuideSys SDK & tracing alignment

Thanks Karthik / Ana —

I can own the SOW logistics and timeline. Quick notes for the call so we can be efficient:

- Goal: agree to a compat-lite checklist + 4-week pilot plan (integration + 2 acceptance tests: telemetry reconciliation & prompt fidelity)
- Deliverables from GuideSys before pilot start: completed compat matrix, sample traces (OTel) for 2 requests, and an export of raw vs rendered prompt examples for 5 templated cases.
- Deliverables from Redwood: a small acceptance harness (runbook + tests), suggested span attributes, and contact points for on-call triage during pilot weeks 2-3.

Timelines:
- Week 0: sign off on compat-lite checklist and SOW (target 4/30)
- Week 1: sandbox wiring + run acceptance harness
- Week 2: run telemetry reconciliation tests; iterate on span attrs
- Week 3-4: acceptance run & go/no-go decision

Ana — can you confirm GuideSys can share the 2 sample traces and 5 templated examples by Fri 2026-04-24 EOD PT? That will let Marissa and Mateo prep the harness.

Vanessa Ortiz
Partner Ops, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: partner-pilot-timeline.xlsx (Excel, 12KB)]

Vanessa / Karthik —

Confirmed. We've uploaded the requested artifacts to the shared Drive folder and attached the trace JSON exports to this message. Notes:
- The templating examples include a control case and four macros that expand to variable-length tokens; we included both raw and rendered forms.
- The traces include request_id and conversation_id; we added a redwood.request_token_count attribute for the sample traces.

Next steps: we'll join the 4/28 call and be prepared to sign the compat-lite checklist on the call if everything looks good. We also accept the proposed 4-week pilot timeline.

Thanks,
Ana Ruiz
